characters.name: Scott Leibfried
characters.description: Badass Arm-Fold: He does as good a job of it as Chef Ramsay. Berserk Button:He tears Andrew Bonito a new one after catching him attempting to evade his team's punishment (having a combination lock put on the door to their storage room) by putting tape on the inside of the door, preventing it from fully closing, furiouslyreiterating that his team was punished because they screwed up, and they must suffer the consequences as opposed to attempting to rig them in their favorbefore taking all the chicken they'd brought to the kitchen back to the storeroom so they'd have to retrieve it again.Contestants who try to take control of the kitchen whenever Ramsay's not around. Just ask Benjamin Knack.Hereallyhates getting reamed by the contestants when they're in control of the kitchen. He got really pissed at Andrea when she got to temporarily run the kitchen and constantly criticized his work endlessly due to overconfidence and expecting all of his dishes to be sabotaged instead of just one or two dishes. It got to the point that he actually insulted and threatened her and thanked Chef Ramsay with relief when he took over again. characters.name: James Avery
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: After being away for Seasons 15-22, he returns for Season 23. The Gadfly: During punishments that involve the blue team eating or drinking something really horrible, he often has a huge grin on his face. Hidden Depths: Along with Andi, he revealed that he's had to make a lot of sacrifices to be a chef and be as successful as he had and that it's really hard to balance work and his personal life with his wife and kids. Put on a Bus: Left in Season 15. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: Like Scott, he's big, bald, and someone who you definitely don't want to get on the wrong side of.

characters.name: Aaron Mitrano
characters.description: Beware the Quiet Ones: While generally more quieter and friendlier than someone like Scott, during the blue team’s punishment in Season 15 episode 12, he is seen by getting annoyed at Frank constantly chattering and boasting about his life in the marines instead of focusing on doing his job. He gets more dissatisfied again during the first dinner service in Season 16 episode 1, with the blue team’s dinner service being a total disaster he comes in the dorms, orders the blue team to return to the kitchen and answers a firm no to Johnny after the latter asks if he can quickly run back to the dorm to put his chef jacket back on. Gentle Giant: Despite his large stature, Aaron was notably calm, reserved, and quiet on the line. He actively chose not to use his size to bully or intimidate contestants. He preferred a peaceful, focused kitchen environment and only raised his voice or used his imposing presence when a contestant's disrespect forced him to. Out of Focus: Doesn't really get much screen time, even when compared to James before him. The Quiet One: Unlike the previous sous chefs on the blue team that appeared before him, Aaron is usually seen as more of reserved and quieter while still following Chef’s Ramsay’s standards. The Stoic: Is one of the most quietest sous chefs on the blue team to date, as well as being the most focused on the job at hand.

characters.name: James "Jocky" Petrie
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: While for the most part he's much more laid-back than his three predecessors, he didn't hesitate to call out Jen on her attitude during Season 18. Hidden Depths: He showed some soccer skills during the All-Stars blue team's second reward when they competed with soccer Olympians. The Stoic: Much more calm and softly-spoken compared to his three predecessors, for the most part. Though he still doesn't hesitate to call out mistakes when he sees them being made.

characters.name: MaryAnnSalcedo
characters.description: Consummate Professional: Deconstructed. One of the main reasons she left the show is due to her annoyance having to work with unprofessional and unskilled contestants. Put on a Bus: Left after the third season, just as the show was starting to become more popular. Red Oni, Blue Oni: Ironically, she's the calmer Blue Oni to Chef Scott's aggressive Red Oni.

characters.name: Gloria Felix
characters.description: Put on a Bus: Was supposed to remain in her role for Seasons 6 and 7, but either quit or was fired at a late stage. The Silent Bob: Very rarely said or did anything of note while on the show, and usually just stood by the pass looking vaguely annoyed.

characters.name: Andi van Willigan
characters.description: Beware the Quiet Ones: Unlike Scott or Ramsay, Andi tends to be the quieter of the brigade; she's stoic but rarely shouts. Until you get her inMommie Dearest-mode. Oh boy. In the few instances she's become annoyed, she'd easily give Scott a run for his money, as Season 12's Anton can attest. The Bus Came Back: Returns as Sous Chef in Season 16. She leaves again next season, where Christina replaces the following season onwards. Character Focus: Since Scott Liebfried left after Season 10, Andi has been getting more focus out of herself and Sous Chefs James and Aaron. During black team services, she's usually the one helping out Chef Ramsay on service and helping test the chefs when they get to run the pass. A Day in the Limelight: Gets a noticeable amount of screen time in Season 12, arguably more so than Scott did during his time. She tells the red team herHidden Depths(see below) during one of their punishments, having an episode at Anton, giving Scott (the contestant) advice when he asks her for some, escorts a winning black jacket contestant to their reward, and tries to convince Joy from quitting in the middle of an ongoing service. Deadpan Snarker: She doesn't have many moments, but she can snark with the best of them.

characters.name: Jean-Philippe Susilovic
characters.description: Berserk Button: He really doesn't like Francisco, the party planner. Beware the Nice Ones: There are times where people push him too far, and he pushes back. One of the best examples of this is his tussle with Van in Episode 2 of Season 6. Butt-Monkey: Often has to deal with irritated customers due to the failures in the kitchen and theEpic Failof some of the contestants. That and Chef Ramsay loves picking on him. Fully morphed into this when he was forced to sumo wrestle with Ramsay. Camp Straight: Often mistaken forCamp Gayby viewers and even some of the contestants, but he confirmed to being heterosexual when indirectly questioned by Season 7's Red Team, and can occasionally be seen flirting with female diners. Commuting on a Bus: Didn't appear from Season 8 until Season 11. It turned out that he was busy opening Gordon's restaurant, Petrus by Gordon Ramsay. He returned for Seasons 11 and 12, only to leaveagainfor Season 13 to move back to his native Belgium.

characters.name: Francisco the Party Planner
characters.description: Blithe Spirit: He's constantly happy and having a good time...even when other competitors get annoyed by him. Camp Gay: Oh so much. LA even refers to him as "parade gay". Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: After the fifth season, he never made an appearance again. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: To Jean-Philippe. Every time Francisco shows up, expect JP to get frustrated with him.

characters.name: James Lukanik
characters.description: Funny Foreigner: Actually born in the UK, though to Eastern European parents. Get a Hold of Yourself, Man!: Does this for Brian when he's kicked out of the kitchen and states that Chef Ramsay needs him to fight back. Brian listens. Suspiciously Similar Substitute:Funny ForeignerMaître d' who's a bit uptight?

characters.name: Marino Monferrato
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Appeared as a challenge judge in Season 11, before taking over as the show's maître d' two seasons later. Butt-Monkey: Subverted. Oftentimes, Ramsay will poke fun at him, as he did with Jean-Philippe, but it usually results in Marino responding by firing back at Ramsay. For example, in Season 22, when Ramsay threw food at him as a joke, Marino immediately did it back in good fun, thus starting a food fight. He also often enjoys doing silly things rather than being the butt of the joke itself, such as appearing in ridiculous costumes like a cowboy or a space suit. Catchphrase: He often saysSi, chef!in place of the usual "Yes, chef!" Deadpan Snarker: He gets to indulge in this in Season 20, snarking at the chefsEpic Failmoments during service.Marino: (During Chickengate when he sees the raw chicken) Come on guys, even the front of house guy can cook it better.Marino: (After returning Megan Ramsay's bland noodles) It tasted nothing like the one she had this morning, so go back to your drawing boards. Funny Foreigner: Marino is Italian and peppers Italian in when he's speaking. He also gets to indulge in antics that JP would never have gotten away with, like trying to catch burnt food that Chef Ramsay was throwing in his direction.

characters.name: Matthew Childs
characters.description: Funny Foreigner: Averted; Matthew is the first American maître d' in the show's history. Temporary Substitute: Fills in the maître d' role while Marino is away visiting family.

characters.name: Jason Thompson
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: Returned in Season 15. Deadpan Snarker: Most of his commentaries come off very ironic in context. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": Even many longtime fans of the show don't even know his name and just refer to him as "the announcer". The Faceless: He is never seen. Pungeon Master: Too many instances to count.

characters.name: Roger Craig Smith
characters.description: Yes,thatRogerCraigSmith. The Voice: Just like Jason, he's only known as such.

characters.name: Moriya Satoru
characters.description: The main protagonist, a third year middle schooler who's got no idea what he wants to do with his life—until a certain demon appears in his life, with the aim of making him be atrue chef, whether he likes it or not. Berserk Button: Especially after befriending Nao of the Agricultural Department, he gets pissed whenever he sees someone wasting food. Beware the Nice Ones: As written below, Satoru is normally a sweet kid. But mess with his friends, waste food, or piss him off in any way, and he will reveal a will of iron. Butt-Monkey: A lot of the manga's comedy revolves around Satoru being tortured by Dogma in an over-the-top way. Character Development: Started out as somebody who gave up easily and always said 'no way' to the point where he was known as 'Noriya' by his friends, gradually becomes somebody who refuses to give up no matter the odds. This also applies to his culinary skills—Satoru goes from somebody who was cooking only because he was forced into it to having his own motivations and reasons for cooking (a large part of the manga is dedicated to Moriya learning why he wants to cook), which is further exemplified by his increasing knowledge and abilities about cooking as the manga carried on.

characters.name: Dogma
characters.description: The Earl of Poor Eating, a demon that loves food and wants to eat the soul of a true chef. He approaches Satoru with the intention of grooming him into a true chef whose soul he can eat after his death. Anti-Hero: Of theNominal Herovariety. Dogma is one of the main characters and essentially the main mentor of Satoru; there's no doubt that without him barging into Satoru's life and forcing him to become a chef, he would have never rechieved theCharacter Developmenthe ended up getting and gained the confidence and love for cooking he has by the end of the manga's run. However, this doesn't change the fact that he's a literal demon of Hell with asociopathicpersonality who wants to eat Satoru's soul and is anUnsympathetic Comedy Protagonistat best. Bad Boss: He constantly treats Satoru like an underling of his. In the first volume he even threatens to feed him to Ghouls if he refuses to obey and his cruel training methods put even someone likeRebornto shame. Berserk Button: Do not claim to be the best in the world, or that there is only one way of cooking. Anyone who has done this in front of him will be challenged to a cooking battle wherehe casually proves them wrong. Chef of Iron: Dogma is by far the best cook in the cast, being fluent in every style of cooking and every form of cuisine. Any cooking battle that he personally takes part in ends with him winning effortlessly.

characters.name: Nakarai Gien
characters.description: A talented and eccentric student of the cooking department with more than a few behavioral issues but talent enough to be considered the best the department has to offer. The Ace: Largely acknowledged as this of the Cooking Department, even by the dean herself. Animal Motifs: Cats. He wears cat mitts and his behavior is very catlike - he comes and goes wherever he wants and can't be corralled to do anything. Brilliant, but Lazy: Is a genius but slacks off if he's not interested in something which is almost always Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Despite his cooky behavior and outlandish ideas, he is considered a genius and hasn't been kicked out because he always aces every test he is given despite never appearing in classes, though he appears again once he decides that Satoru is his rival.

characters.name: Morisaki Yoh
characters.description: A student from the first year of Shokusen. An intense young man with no particular specialty when it comes to food, but gravitates towards meat dishes. Badass Normal: Although good in his own right, he definitely lacks the crazier skills of his peers and their skills, so he mostly cooks like a normal cook rather than using any particular skill. Big Brother Instinct: Comes naturally when one is the eldest sibling out of seven,as portrayed when he finds out his little brother became a delinquent. It occasionally widens to include Satoru and the others(such as Gien), although he mostly treats them as friends. Butt-Monkey: He tends to get the short end of the stick more often than not. He's only after Satoru in the amount of times that Dogma caused pain to someone, a lot of it because Dogma finds him annoying. Comic Relief: He isn't very used for intense or serious scenes, most of his time is dedicated to be in some joke to lighten the mood of the manga.

characters.name: Akiyama Elle
characters.description: A shy and sweet girl, daughter of the owner of a Chinese restaurant, she always holds a huge wok and hides behind it when she feels threatened, which is almost all the time. Her specialty is making fried rice in her wok. Animal Motif: Frogs. During the match against the Science Department, she is called frog-chan, frogs are her favorite animal and she is always wearing a frog pin in her head. Bespectacled Cutie: She is a very shy and polite girl who wears large round glasses. Character Development: While maintaining a status ofShrinking Violet, she is much more headstrong and determinated in matches after meeting and befriending Satoru. Daddy's Girl: She loves her father and his cooking, she enters the school with the intention of bettering the image of his cooking after the restaurant starts facing strong competition and losing business.

characters.name: Tachibana Kei
characters.description: A strange and eccentric man that believes spices can rule over cooking. He has an extremely developed nose, capable of smelling things and using spices to a whole new level. His specialty are dishes heavy on spices, such as curry. Abusive Parents: His father was never even mentioned and his mother would mostly ignore him, feeding him nothing but cup noodles and frozen meals, because she couldn't be bothered to cook for him. She eventually went missing and left her child behind. Anti-Hero: Easily the most morally grey character in the story, Kei is a rather cold and deadpan person with lone wolf tendencies and trust issues that cause him to mistrust even those he considers friends. He is also very competative and eventurned evilat one point. However, despite his flaws, he's ultimately good deep down and his time as an antagonist lasts for only one arc. Character Development: He rechieves this more than any other character in the series besides Satoru himself. At the beginning of his arc, Kei is portrayed as a cynical, dismissive, and emotionally distant lone wolf. His perspective that cooking is worthless stems from profound childhood experiences, particularly with his mother, who treated him as an annoyance and ultimately abandoned him. This foundational neglect fosters distrust and resentment within Kei, making him wary of establishing connections with others, including his friends. Eventually he has aFace–Heel Turn, turning against his friends, joining the Science Department and participating in its plan to undermine and destroy cooking while having an even further descent into nihilism. However, thanks to Satoru's influence, the joy, creativity, and communal aspects of cooking, elements that Kei has tried to deny throughout the Battle Of The Five Senses Arc, His character arc concludes with an appreciation for cooking, turning towards a middle ground where he can value culinary arts without the weight of past traumas weighing him down, ultimately refusing to join

characters.name: Minami Sagane
characters.description: A cheerful and romantic girl who is obsessed with knives, and has a crush on Satoru. She has over 200 different knives that she has the skills and knowledge to use in her cooking, and her knifework is impeccable—both in and out of the kitchen. Her speciality is decorative carving, such as character bentos. A-Cup Angst: Padding is the only reason she even passes as an A-Cup, something that's a bit of a sore spot for her. Anti-Hero: As part of the cooking department and thus, Satoru's friend group, Minami is also part of the main cast. She's also aBlade EnthusiastYanderewith an unhealthy crush on Satoru who's consistantly portrayed as a danger to others and has murderous intents towards anyone she perceives as a threat to their "relationship". Blade Enthusiast: Like you wouldn't believe. She has 200 knives and counting, all with different names and uses. She's protective of all of them, treating them like her own kids, and anyone who touches them without her permission gets knives thrown at them, no matter how well meaning they are. Yandere:For Satoru. She was willing to steal knives for him and go after Hakka with her knives.She attempts to kill Akiyama in the Hell Island Arc because she thought Akiyama was Satoru's boyfriend thanks to a previous arc, although they quickly come to an understanding afterwards.

characters.name: Levi Golgotha
characters.description: The rich son of the Golgotha family, a rich family of candy suppliers. His specialty is in making sweets, which he excels at. He loves women and tries to gather a group to be part of his personal troupe. Does Not Like Men: He wishes to be surrounded by women and hates to be around men, in fact, he even hates the idea of men eating his dishes, specially since he learned to cook to impress women. French Cuisine Is Haughty: He is a french chef, with a knack for sweets. His dishes are always very high class with several techniques executed masterfully. In fact, he first makes an Opera cake, a french pastry particularly known for it's high-class style and difficulty. French Jerk: He is from France and is quite the unflattering person, he mostly mistreats the men around him and tries to get the women to be into him. Non-Uniform Uniform: Instead of the usual pants, he wears gray and blue plaid shorts together with knee-high socks.

characters.name: Kumoi Mitsuroh
characters.description: A 2nd year known for his ruthless and harsh behavior towards all other chefs and being very selective of the people he allows to contract him, but known for being able to create dishes that can make all his clients feel better by using medicinal principles of Chinese philosophies, which is his specialty. Animal Motif: Crabs. He is called to have the hair of a crab and is constantly chewing on crabs. Anti-Hero: Of theNominal Herovariety. He's consistantly portrayed as a cold and uncaringJerkasswho's disrespectful to everyone. Jerkass: Whenever someone is bellow his expectations, he reacts brutally. Tragic Keepsake: His knife case used to belong to Kuroda, hisParental Substituteand personal chef of his house, who took care of him while he was sick, after Kuroda being fired and his subsequent death, Kumoi took the case and decided to become a chef.

characters.name: Matsuo Mikazuki
characters.description: A high-strung 1st year from Sanuki, Shikoku Island,who blusters mean wordsin an attemptto hide his insecurities. He mellows out when it comes to Udon, which he considers hissoul food, and his specialty. Dark and Troubled Past: It's implied that a lot of his blustering and insecurity is because he used to be bullied. He was nicknamed Garbage Bag as a kid, had no friends until he met Satoru, and based off how he reacted when Satoru says that he thinks Mikazuki's way of thinking about Udon is cool, him being made fun of for liking Udon isn't that farfetched a guess either. Jerkass: In his first appearance, he chops down the sacred tree of the agriculture club and frames Satoru for it. Further appearances tone this down, however, and it's implied that it's because of his insecurities and anxiety. The Napoleon: To the point that his wish in theHot Springs Chapterwas to grow taller.Despite attempts at working out, he's the shortest out of all the male characters, standing tall at 156cm.Justified, as the reason he wants to grow bigger is to gain the strength necessary to knead udon dough without relying on someone. Odd Friendship: With Levi. He's a high-strung Tsundere who specialises in Udon, a savoury dish, while Levi is arich kidwho specialises in sweets. Makes more sense when you consider that both Levi and Mikazuki haveFriendless Background—Levi uses his money to attract groupies instead of friendsandMikazuki is implied to have been bullied as a kid.They bond when tasked to light a fire together during the Hell Island Arc, and a lot of their appearances afterwards are them together, trying to combine chocolate and udon into a tasty recipe.

characters.name: Goshima Himari
characters.description: A cheerful 1st year girl who has nothing but bread on the brain, to the point where her nickname is Bread Crazy. She specialises in baking bread.

characters.name: Utsurogi Mongo
characters.description: A mischievous teenager with a theatrical flair who specialises in B-class cuisine, mostly street-stalls. He's the third son of the Utsurogi group, aYakuzaorganisation stationed in the Kantou Region's Kyoto Parliament, and is the leader of Urameshi, a group that runs festival stalls. He's never seen without a festival mask.Joins Shokusen as a First Year student after the Festival Battle. Animal Motif: Foxes. His festival mask iskitsune-themed, and personality-wise, he can be bothteasinganddangerous, which are often associated with foxes. Impossibly Cool Weapon: A cooking version of the trope. Okonomiyaki spatulas are pretty ordinary, especially for what he tends to be cooking. Okonomiyaki spatulas that are reinforced with enhanced ceramic and connected by a chain over twice his body length, that heuses in a kusarigama-like way to break bladesand cook, however? It more than counts as a part of this trope. Loophole Abuse:Part of the terms for losing the match between him and Kumoi was to never show his face around Kumoi again. Cue wearing a mask whenever he's around Kumoi—literally not showing his face to Kumoi. Sweet Tooth: He's never seen withoutKawarinbo lollipops, and his first appearance is him surrounded by snacks and sweets of all kinds.

characters.name: Inukai Nao
characters.description: The Ace: Of the Agricultural department. Her rice is legendary and the treasure of the department. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: In her introductory chapter, she gets angry at Satoru for anInnocently Insensitivecomment and puts him through a bunch of abuse. However, once Satoru realizes his mistake, they become friends, though she remains a stoic person. The Stoic: She has a cold and deadpan personality. Stripperific: She has a tendency of wearing rather revealing outfits

characters.name: Ichinose Hakka
characters.description: Cloud Cuckoolander: Hakka lives in her own world and barely notices or cares about anything that's not food The Pollyanna: Barely notices when she's being bullied and is always happy especially when there's good food Out of Focus: In the first third or so of the manga due to not being a student at Shokusen and despite being Moriya'sLove Interest. It eases a bit when she joins Shokusen's service department though she still gets less focus due to not being a chef. Unskilled, but Strong: A Michelin acknowledged food critic and blogger despite not having any formal training. She just genuinely loves eating and learned though experience.

characters.name: Saionji Mai
characters.description: The Nicknamer: She always puts nicknames on the people she meets, especially her opponents.

characters.name: Tojo Uraji
characters.description: Jerkass: Unlike the other students in the applied biology department, he genuinely enjoys cooking, but simply refuses to cook for people he considers "ignorant".

characters.name: Kitakata Hidetsugu
characters.description: Foil: To Nakarai. Nakarai is an eccentricCloud Cuckoolanderwhile Kitakata is a stick-in-the-mudJerkass. Jerkass: He is arrogant and considers anyone with lack of intelligence as "monkeys".

characters.name: Sena Touka
characters.description: Foil: To Nakarai asThe AceCloud Cuckoolanderof the science department. Child Prodigy: Accepted on the academy at the age of 8, she also works at NASA making astronaut food. The Eeyore: Constantly depressed and unmotivated, she is always trying to commit suicide, none of her attempts work, however.

characters.name: Nakagame Naomi
characters.description: Big Good: As the Dean of the cooking department, she's portrayed as the overall leader of the cooking department students as well as it's teachers. Red Oni, Blue Oni: Her hot-blooded personality makes the complete opposite of Sakaki who despite hisStern Teachertendencies, is pretty much theOnly Sane Manof the whole school staff.

characters.name: Sakaki Hajime
characters.description: Badass Biker: Owns a bike that shoots out flames that he uses to cook Cloudcuckoolander's Minder: Is generally theOnly Sane Manamongst the teachers and is constantly scolding Nakarai. Cuteness Overload: Apparently, all true delinquents would never harm children and small animals Japanese Delinquents: Was once the delinquent and occasionally relapses. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: His POV chapter makes it clear that he genuinely cares about the future of his students and wants them to reach the top. Cooking department students are shown in the same chapter being fully aware of it which is why they like him despite hisStern Teachertendencies.

characters.name: Kuga Masumi
characters.description: Extreme Doormat: Is easily bullied by his students who make fun of him and take over his office. Friend to All Children: Became a teacher because he wanted children to enjoy his snacks and believes that confections should be available to all Long Neck: Is draw with a long neck because he's associated withgiraffesas cute cartoon animals for children. Nice Guy: He's easily the nicest out of all the teacher characters in the series and is never shown being stern or raising his voice. Understatement: Kuga once "participated in a private competition and came in last". It was a world baking competition and Kuga broke records but got disqualified on a technicality.

characters.name: Kaide Matsuchi
characters.description: Cloud Cuckoo Lander: His rough cowboyesque personality has lead to moments like riding a horse in-doors, for example. He's also least technical out of all the teachers as he can only tell if food tastes "delicious or not". Living Legend: Is hailed by the Agriculture Department as a sort of God—according to them, anywhere the Dean sleeps means the area is particularly good to the products that are being raised there, and guaranteed a bountiful harvest for the next three years.

characters.name: Sakata Majorica
characters.description: Ambiguous Gender: Identifies as both man and woman, implying the possibility of being bi-gender.

characters.name: Yuri Dragunov
characters.description: Affably Evil: Although he is extremely vocal of his distaste for cuisine and eccentric to the highest degree, he isn't really mean and genuinely believes he is doing good. Big Bad: Of the Science Department Arc, being the one luringTachibanato join them and leading the team against the main group. The Corruptor:To Tachibana. Heel–Face Turn: After the Battle of the Five Senses, he gives up his plan to destroy the concept of cooking from the world and becomes a part of the manga's regular cast alongside the rest of his department. Knight of Cerebus: His arc severly darkens the mood of the manga. While he has a ton of comedic moments, thanks to his weird personality, Dragunov is still portrayed as scarily competantMad Scientistwho wants to destroy the very concept of the story's defining theme all whilecorrupting Tachibana into his way of thinking, briefly turning him into a massively nihilisticJerkassas a result.

characters.name: Beelzebub
characters.description: Big Bad: He's the main villain of the manga's very short-lived Heavenly Chef Course Arc. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: He makes the (very false) assumption that Dogma and Satoru have a genuine bond of friendship and love and mocks them for it. Faux Affably Evil: During his attack on Dogma, he acts like he's meeting an old friend. However, it's quickly made clear that he's evil to the core. Karma Houdini: Thanks to the manga being cancelled just as his arc was getting started, Beelzebub never gets any comeuppence for his unprovoked attack on Dogma. Knight of Cerebus: He's easily the darkest villain in the whole manga, (even compared to Dragunov) being it's only demon antagonist. For one thing, he's is capable of hurting Dogma who, also being a demon, has superhuman physical characteristics. It's clear that had his arc gotten to continue, it would have been the most serious one in tone.

characters.name: Season  1
characters.description: The Ace: Outside of a few instances in the beginning, he was one of the most consistent chefs this season. Best shown when he was moved to the Red Team in Episode 3 and helped them to start winning services. He also won while never being nominated for elimination, a feat he shares with Season 2's Heather,Season 5's Danny,Season 6's Dave, Season 7's Holli,Season 10's Christina,Season 13's La Tasha, Season 14's Meghan,Season 16's Ryan,Season 18's Ariel,andSeason 22's Ryan. Actually a Good Idea: His pass sabotage on Ralph. He managed to expose some of Ralph's weak points as a leader, while managing to get away with it because Ralph should've noticed it, and Gordon actually admitted it was a clever move. Notably, this would result in the pass sabotages that would occur every season since. Best Friend: With Jimmy. Beware the Quiet Ones: Was quite soft-spoken. But of all the winners inHell's Kitchen, he was the most cutthroat of them all, not afraid to sabotage others or nominate strong competitors for elimination (back when Chef Ramsay was unable to override nominations). Born Lucky: Michael holds the distinction of being safe in all of the team services for the first six episodes having been on the winning team for five services and the one time he was on the losing team, he was Best Of The Worst.

characters.name: Season  2
characters.description: The Ace: While she did have some struggles midway through the season, Heather was overall the best chef of the season, only ever being beaten in individual challenges while crushing most services and being the best leader of the season by a large margin. This allowed her to achieve victory without being nominated, a feat shared with Season 1's Michael,Season 5's Danny,Season 6's Dave, Season 7's Holli,Season 10's Christina,Season 13's La Tasha, Season 14's Meghan,Season 16's Ryan,Season 18's Ariel,andSeason 22's Ryan. Always Someone Better: During the Black Jacket phase of the competition she frequently got despondent about how she always poured her heart and soul into what she was making during the challenges, and yet Virginia effortlessly blew her out of the water each time. Averted when it really mattered, however, as Heather defeated Virginia in the final service. Berserk Button:As Garret found out, making any sexist comments in her direction will immediately get you on her bad side.For the most part she was a nice girl. But after a while, Virginia brought out a nasty side of hers since Heather felt likeVirginia was treated unfairly well. She lightened up a lot on this when they moved into the finals together however. As Garret found out, making any sexist comments in her direction will immediately get you on her bad side. For the most part she was a nice girl. But after a while, Virginia brought out a nasty side of hers since Heather felt likeVirginia was treated unfairly well. She lightened up a lot on this when they moved into the finals together however.

characters.name: Season  3
characters.description: Berserk Button: Having to sort through trash causes him to have a complete meltdown, due to it reminding him of his childhood in the ghetto. Beware the Nice Ones: He grew up in the ghetto and never had to go dumpster diving, so when losing a challenge meant he had to sort through trash he lost it to the pointTelevision Without Pitygave him his own bleep o fucking meter. Later, he shows regret over the act, and more or less goes back to being normal for the remainder of the season. He crossed into this territory again for the first Black Jacket service, when he became very irritable and picked fights with Jen and Bonnie. After elimination that night, he cooled off and apologized to Jen for his behavior. Breakout Character: Of a sort, as he's one of the few winners to make more than one appearance in future seasons. Brutal Honesty: Was fairly blunt when he voiced his opinions on how weak Josh was. Right in front of him. Deadpan Snarker: One of the best examples inHell's Kitchenhistory.Rock:(about Susan in Season 11)The woman with the towel on her head wasn't too intimidating. I think we're good.

characters.name: Season  4
characters.description: Aloof Ally: Sometimes had shades of this given the dislike she immediately encountered from most of the Red Team, as well as her habit of carrying herself in a very controlled and quiet manner. Also, she stated that she didn't care about her teammates at one point, and only cared about finishing a service. Bash Brothers: With Corey; they bickered a lot, and even nominated each other after the final three service. But when picking their teams for the final service, Christina (who had second choice) was worried that Petrozza would choose Corey first, and it even seemed that Corey was worried about it (but Petrozza picked Bobby). They personally disliked each other, but worked very well together in service. Batman Gambit: After Jen rigged the nomination votes, she works out with Corey and Petrozza who the strongest of them is, forcing Ramsay to eliminate Jen instead of Corey. Breakout Character: Much like Rock, she has made numerous appearances in future seasons of the show. Brutal Honesty: In the season finale, she openly dissedHell's Kitchen'sdefault decor to the face of the show's production designer (i.e. the person who selected said decor). For an encore, she was similarly scathing with the options for serving staff outfits that Jean-Philippe presented her.

characters.name: Season  5
characters.description: The Ace: Easily one of the strongest chefs of the season, being the only chef of his season to completely avoid nomination. Achilles' Heel: Was consistently great at nearly every station he worked. But the station he hated the most was the garnish station, performing rather badly on his first night on it. He managed to improve (got awarded Best Of The Worst status on his second night on garnish), but he still had a little trouble with it on the third night. Badass Boast: Was an absolute MASTER of these.Danny:A lot of chefs get up here, and they say this is all they know how to do. You know what?Fuck that chef.This is all I want to do. You know that I have what it takes to run the restaurant Borgata.Danny:I'm here to fight to the bitter end. Watch out because I'm bringing the heat! Badasses Wear Bandanas: Wore one in every service. Bash Brothers: With Ben; they started off on a sour note (with Ben saying Danny "couldn't cook his cock") and things were often tense between them, but they ALWAYS had each other's backs in the kitchen. During the finale, Ben was Danny's first pick for his team.

characters.name: Season  6
characters.description: The Ace: Oh so much; he never had even one dinner service that was only "pretty good". He was also never once nominated by his teammates. Achilles' Heel: Crepes were one for him — when he presented one in the health food challenge, Ramsay actuallylaughed out loudas soon as he saw how small it was, and then said that it tasted foul. On that occasion it was implied that Andy was more at fault for how the crepe turned out, but Dave had no excuses when he presented an even worse one three episodes later, which Ramsay likened to diarrhea and refused to even taste. Ascended Fanboy: Idolized Chef Ramsay for years. One of his top priorities was to earn his respect. He accomplished that goal as he was one of the most impressive chefs in the show's entire run. Badass Boast: Gave some pretty good ones when dealing with his arm, like in Episode 13 when he recalled how he almost passed out from the pain and Chef Ramsay forced him to visit the medic (he later claimed that he had never seen a chef in so much pain).Dave:I'm not a quitter and I'm not a wuss. No matter how messed up my wrist is, I can take the pain and I'm here to stay.Another one during the craps challenge:Dave:I picked figs with fish and we won. Another one during the craps challenge:

characters.name: Season  7
characters.description: The Ace: She, along with Jay, were the only two chefs that season to completely avoid nomination. Badass Adorable: Hollie looks good and is one of the biggest sweethearts of the competition. She is also one of the stronger links of the red team who managed to win the competition. Bittersweet Ending: Despite winning the competition, she was unable to take the job at the Savoy in London due to work permit problems, causing her to accuse the show's producers of never having had any intention of employing her.noteIn actual fact, the UK's immigration laws at the time required any vacancy to have been advertised to UK or European Union nationals before it could be offered to anyone else. Since the vacancy was a prize in a TV show it wasn't technically advertisedat all, and thus didn't meet the requirements for Holli to be given a UK work permit. This was apparently the result of the show's production staff not realizing the law had changed since Season 1, when Michael was offered the opportunity to work at Gordon Ramsay's flagship restaurant in London.Though she would go on to find success after the show, creating her own line of cookware and opening her own organic farm. The Cameo: Made one for the 100th dinner service in Season 8. Chekhov's Gunman: An interesting real-life example. As seen under herOut of Focussection, she never got a lot of focus throughout the competition, and wasn't even treated like an actual threat due to Jay, Benjamin, and even Autumn and Ed displaying more promise. Come the black jackets however, Holli would start to get more focus and actually became a massive threat to win, and sure enough, she did.

characters.name: Season  8
characters.description: Cordon Bleugh Chef: Played straight with her Signature Dish, which was fried chicken with undercooked asparagus. The secret to her chicken was that she put all seasonings in first; unfortunately,honeywas one of them. Ramsay was not impressed. Completely averted from that point onward though, as her palate ultimately won him over by the end. Deadpan Snarker: She has her moments of this. The earliest example was her reaction to Emily and her boobs. 11th-Hour Superpower: Was nominated twice during the middle of the competition and had some shaky services in the latter half of the season, but emerged as the best of the group towards the end thanks to her strong palate and decent leadership skills. Formerly Fat: Easily the largest person to have wonHell's Kitchen, and looked much the same when she made a guest appearance early in Season 9, but when she returned again in Season 11 she had lost a significant amount of weight. Considering she had just had a baby during Season 8, it's likely she had simply gained some weight following that and lost it by the time of Season 11. Genre Blind: Following the third service, she tried to shield Melissa from elimination by persuading the other women to nominate one person (Emily) based on the service, and one person (Sabrina) based on the pre-service prep work, despite the fact that Ramsay almost never takes prep into consideration when eliminating people, and Sabrina hadn't even been in the kitchen (which a baffled Ramsay himself pointed out when Sabrina was nominated). In the end though, it didn't matter much because Emily had been far worse than either Melissa or Sabrina... and Raj in turn had been so spectacularly awful that Ramsay booted him out despite the Blue Team winning that night.

characters.name: Season  9
characters.description: Achilles' Heel: While Paul was one of the best chefs on the blue team and ended up with the win, he royally screwed up fish on the sixth service, which resulted in his only nomination. Subverted in the seventh service, when he covered for the ejected Natalie on fish and managed to redeem himself from last night's poor performance. On his third time on the fish station, he sent up an overcooked lobster tail, but thankfully, it was not enough for nomination as everybody else looked towards Elise and Jennifer. Angrish: He delves into this as he reams out Chino and Brendan for their mistakes in the second service, being unable to finish his sentence. Arch-Enemy: Early on in the competition, he was this for Brendan, as Paul disliked his overly cocky attitude while not being able to back it up in the kitchen. The feud petered out after Brendan's early elimination. Ass Shove: Was on the receiving end of this. While sticking his head out of the limo on a reward, Will got the bright idea to shove the bottle he was holding up his ass. Paul's response was to accidentally knock the bottle onto Will. Awesome Ego: Outside of the one instance he was nominated, Paul was usually able to back up his bragging extremely well.

characters.name: Season  10
characters.description: The Ace: Throughout the competition, She rarely if ever screwed up in either challenges or services. This all culminated in her winning the competition and, years later, becoming the Red Team's sous chef. Actually Pretty Funny: In Season 22 (The American Dream), she bursts out into laughter upon discovering the Red Team had screwed up a punishment by churning butter over ice, causing them to have to do more work than necessary. Beware the Nice Ones:While a nice person overall, she nearly hit her limit during the Fashion Night punishment due to spending hours carrying heavy risers and even snapping at Dana.She was not impressed with Tiffany's outburst towards Barbie on Family Night, and voted her for elimination based on how unprofessional she had acted.She's one of the nicer Sous Chefs, and gets along with almost everyone. That being said, she isn't afraid to verbally thrash anyone she considers a troublemaker - as Season 15's Jackie finds out the hard way.In Season 18 (Rookies Vs. Veterans), she verbally ripped the Rookies a new one for arriving late for prep, even asking if they were on vacation time.In Season 19 (Las Vegas), she tore Jordan, Mary Lou, and Fabiola a new one for not only joking around during a punishment when they knew she was pissed at them, but doing it at a punishment at the restaurantsheis the head chef at. While a nice person overall, she nearly hit her limit during the Fashion Night punishment due to spending hours carrying heavy risers and even snapping at Dana. She was not impressed with Tiffany's outburst towards Barbie on Family Night, and voted her for elimination based on how unprofessional she had acted.

characters.name: Season  11
characters.description: Berserk Button: Understandably, she didn't take too kindly to being considered for nomination in the latter stages of the competition, when the other three remaining women were clearly gunning for her. Less so in Episode 13, the one occasion where she had a truly bad performance; she said that while she thought Susan should be up (fortunately for her, Cyndi and Mary agreed on without hesitation), she would accept being nominated if that was what the Red Team decided. Bittersweet Ending: Was prevented from taking the winners' job due to undisclosed reasonsnoteallegedly due to failing a narcotics test., though she did later become the Executive Chef at Corner Table in her hometown ofHouston, TX, but only for a year. Complexity Addiction: Lampshaded by Nedra, but Ja'Nel had a habit of coming up with some odd ideas for dishes, with them varying on whether or not they came out right. The Generic Girl: She didn't stand that much out personality wise in comparison to the other colorful contestants. Out of Focus: For the first half of the season, she didn't have much screen presence. But as time went on, she started establishing herself as a badass by dominating in the challenges. Emerged more by entering the Black Jackets, then winning Hell's Kitchen.

characters.name: Season  12
characters.description: Accentuate the Negative: This would often be how Scott would be put up for nomination. While other chefs would make much more costly mistakes, they or other chefs would say Scott's mistakes were worse than theirs, resulting in Scott being put up for relatively minor mistakes in the long run. The Ace: Specifically in terms of his leadership, which is critical in the late-game competition. While he was a good cook and many of his nominations were unfair, he made his share of mistakes in the kitchen compared to the other top chefs from the season. However, Scott had arguably the best pass performance ever in the series and was practically perfect in commanding his brigade. As such, a strong case can be made for him being the best leader in the show's history. Beware the Nice Ones: Admitted how frustrated he was in Episode 17 of constantly being railed on by everybody and he eventually snapped...at Chef Ramsay. He very nearly got thrown out on the spot and barely avoided elimination that night. Happens again in the finale, where he tosses Jessica out of service for her constantly forgetting even basic cooking standards - one of the few finalists to ever do so. Breakout Character: Much like Rock, Paul, and both Christinas, he's made appearances in future seasons, even being a guest diner for one service. Butt-Monkey:Some of his nominations were debatable, such as Episode 11, where he made no mistakes and even scored the winning point in the challenge. However, he was nominated over Gabriel, who served frozen mushrooms.It happened again in Episode 14. His only mistakes were slicing and serving a plate of raw chicken (that was cooked by Anton) and attempting to cook a full order of scallops when Chef Ramsay only asked for a single scallop to complete a full dish (the scallops were saved thanks to Anton and Kashia noticing on time and removing the pan from the heat), yet he was nominated over Kashia, who had some mistakes in the fish station.

characters.name: Season  13
characters.description: The Ace: Easily the strongest chef of the season, barely having a service that was below sub-standard and, outside of her signature dish, was a consistent and strong chef. Bifauxnen: Whenever the red team goes out to dinner for rewards, she's always dressed in a pantsuit. Book Dumb: "I don't know what 'lacks-a-daisical' is, but when I find out, I'm gonna make sure toneverbe it again."notemeans "lacking enthusiasm and determination", something that La Tasha probably can’t be accused of being. Deadpan Snarker: She had her moments of this. Epic Fail: Was an amazing chef throughout the competition... except for her signature dish, which was just a piece of grilled watermelon that was underwhelming! It just goes to show that the signature dishes aren't necessarily indicative of how well a chef will perform.

characters.name: Season  14
characters.description: The Ace: Oh so much. Rarely has a chef dominated their season to the extent that she had. In particular during services, where she had asingleinstance of a mistake, which was corrected very quickly.That instance being in Episode 14, where she was preparingfourteensteaks simultaneously, and accidentally sent uponeraw New York striploin. Even Ramsay is in disbelief when he points out her mistake, saying "Of all the people." However, unlike many chefs who derail after a mistake, she instantly recovers, and has no future issues.Challenge wise, she was also strong, if only not quite as strong as services. Despite having to endure more punishments than most contestants ever, her team's losses wereneverdue to her (at least not explicitly; she never sunk the team with a dreadful performance), and she always performed adequately if not the best. characters.name: Season  15
characters.description: Consummate Professional: Despite her mutual dislike of Kristin, they work together well in the kitchen. Determinator: Refuses to let a broken foot keep her out of the competition, like Dave from season 6 with his hand. Don't Celebrate Just Yet: She has this mindset upon reaching the final three, saying that while she is excited to make the top three, she wouldn't be celebrating until she won. Handicapped Badass: She injures her foot in episode 7 and opts to remain in the competition by wearing a compression boot, meaning that she has to do prep work sitting down and can't really move much from her station during dinner service. In the same episode, despite the service being disastrous, Ariel makes no mistakes in her cooking and it's only thanks to her taking charge that the Red Team is (barely) able to complete service. Afterwards, despite a few bumps, she has remained consistently one of the strongest chefs on her team despite her injured leg. Hypocrite: Nominated Vanessa for elimination after the third service, telling Chef Ramsay that she wasn't a team player. This may have had more weight, had Ariel not overridden the team consensus of Manda in order to nominate Vanessa.
